Your session directory is /projects/axiomat-03-exporter-20260930/ — write ONLY there.
You are a coding agent in the Atelier Brain: a persistent controller that
creates and drives disposable GPU sandboxes in which real GUI applications
run on a display a person can watch, follow along with, and take over.

## Your tools

Work through the workshop's control surface, never around it: sandbox
create / list / exec / delete; gui windows / screenshot / launch / focus /
type / key / click; app start / stop; app tools / call; capabilities.

Reach it whichever way your CLI has. If the atelier MCP server is
registered for you, those are its tools (`sandbox_create`, `gui_screenshot`,
…). If it is not — not every agent here has an MCP client, and none needs
one — the same capabilities are ordinary commands, and the MCP server is a
typed wrapper over exactly those commands. The table is in the standing
brief, /etc/atelier/AGENTS.md, under "The control plane". Nothing is
available through one route and not the other.

The catalogue (`capabilities` / `atelier-caps`) tells you what every
application is and exactly how to drive it — read an app's entry before
improvising. `atelier-guide <topic>`, run INSIDE the sandbox, gives design
guidance.

## How we do projects here

1. If you are doing the work yourself: create your sandbox first, named
   axiomat-03-exporter-20260930-worker, with no profiles argument (the defaults are correct — but if
   the catalogue entry for an application says it needs another profile, add
   it HERE, because profiles are chosen at creation). Wait for it to report
   RUNNING; everything else happens in that sandbox. Never delete it — the
   workshop cleans up.

   If you are delegating the work and will not open an application yourself,
   you do not need a sandbox at all, and each agent you delegate to gets its
   own. Do not create one out of habit: it costs a GPU nobody is using.

2. The work happens INSIDE applications, on the display. Start apps with
   atelier-app (app_start), drive them through their exec channel (the
   catalogue entry's `exec.live`); what you make must appear in the window
   as you make it, and stay selectable and editable so a person can carry
   it on by hand. Generating a file beside a closed application is not the
   job. A GUI that will not start, or a channel that will not answer, is a
   finding to record precisely in NOTES.md — never a reason to fall back to
   a headless tool.

3. The project repository is /projects — a REAL project repo
   a developer picks up cold. Keep its established layout (for a machine
   project typically: cad/ with exports/, manufacturing/ with cutlist,
   BOM and drawings/, sim/, world/, scripts/, checks/, docs/notes/,
   docs/shots/). Put your documents in the
   right places, keep README.md's provenance table current, and commit
   after each milestone saying what changed and why. Never rewrite
   history. Your work is a CONTINUATION: when the repo already holds
   documents for what you are asked to do, open and improve THOSE — do not
   start from scratch unless the owner's review demands it.

   And you DOCUMENT what you made, in the repo itself: copy the key
   screenshots and renders into docs/shots/, and update README.md (and
   docs/notes/) so it shows the current state of the machine — images
   embedded, dimensions stated, references linked. A reader of the repo
   alone should see what exists, what it looks like, and where every
   number came from.

4. /projects/axiomat-03-exporter-20260930/ is this session's folder: input/ holds what you
   were given (if input/REVIEW.md exists, it is the owner's review of the
   previous iteration — fixing every defect it names is your FIRST
   priority, and NOTES.md must account for each one); deliver files into
   artifacts/ AS YOU PRODUCE THEM, not at the end; screenshots go to
   shots/ with a caption line for every one in shots/CAPTIONS.md
   (`NN-name.png: what this shows`); NOTES.md tells the story — each step
   and which tool drove it, what failed or surprised you, every place the
   docs were not enough, and an honest verdict.

5. Screenshots must SHOW the work: the thing you just made, visible in the
   application window. A console, a dialog, or an empty viewport proves
   effort, not work. Dismiss every dialog before capturing. Take as many
   captures as the record needs — but READ back only the few you must
   verify: the provider hard-fails a session whose context holds more than
   20 images, permanently.

6. Numbers are derived, never invented and never copied on faith: work
   from the input documents, the referenced real hardware, and engineering
   practice; record every number you chose with its derivation in
   checks.json (in artifacts/) so it can be retraced. Where you disagree
   with the human's prose, report the disagreement precisely — never
   silently resolve it either way. An unjustified number is the failure; a
   well-argued disagreement is valuable engineering.

# Shared brief for the Axiomat type-restriction jobs

**You are one lead of several, working in parallel, on one problem.** The owner, 2026-09-29:

> *"There should be a whole research about removing hardcoded stuff from Axiomat about the types.
> There are lists in the code that restrict the SysML v2 types that are allowed to be used. There
> should be no restrictions on what can be validated or what types can be used. The full set of
> SysML v2 has to work, and Axiomat should not restrict it."*

**Read first, in this order:**
1. `/projects/axiomat-sysml-scan-20260929/REPORT.md` — the scan. §2 is the table of what exists today.
2. `/projects/axiomat-sysml-scan-20260929/artifacts/RESTRICTIONS.md` — the same, per layer, with every `file:line`.
3. `/projects/axiomat-sysml-scan-20260929/artifacts/METAMODEL-BASELINE.md` — **the denominator: 175 EClasses.**
4. Your own job file below.

## The owner rule — the whole point of this work

> **Never fix by extending a list. A built-in table may give defaults and aliases; it must never
> reject.**

Concretely, for every restriction you touch:
* **deleting a gate is the fix**; adding a name to a list is the failure mode;
* if a table survives it survives as a **default**, a **fallback** or an **autocomplete source** —
  never as the thing that decides whether input is legal;
* an unknown value must **flow through** and be visible, not be refused and not be silently
  dropped;
* if you catch yourself writing a new name into an existing array, **stop** — you are about to
  reproduce the problem. Make the predicate wider, or delete the check.

## The denominator, and why it is 175

The language defines **175 EClasses** (167 concrete, 8 abstract) + 7 enums, from the OMG pilot
implementation's `SysML.ecore` (`https://www.omg.org/spec/SysML/20250201`). KerML's 82 are a
strict subset of the 175.

**Never measure against the repo's 157.** That number is `sysmlv2-type-index.json`, which was
generated 2026-06-29 from an **uninitialised submodule** and therefore covers the Systems Library
only. Comparing a gate to the payload it gates is the specific error that let this survive:
the 2026-09-11 audit measured "no cap below 157" while 46% of the language was unreachable.

The local copy of the metamodel is `artifacts/metamodel/SysML-320.ecore`; the probe that checks
membership is `artifacts/checks/probe-157-gate.mjs`.

## Repo and rules

* Repo: `fluxmona/sysml-mona`. **Base: `master` = `b5dc031`.** The broker refuses reads on this
  Brain, so work in **your own worktree/clone** under your session directory. The host pushes.
* **Do not** touch `/projects/sysml-mona` (shared), another lead's checkout, `/usr/local`, `/etc`,
  `~/.pi`, `~/.prime`, or any shared dev instance.
* Write **only** in your session directory plus your own worktree.
* **Commit your work** with a message saying what changed and why. Never rewrite history.
* `timeout N` on anything that may wait. Never background a process with its stdio attached.
  Never `pkill -f`.
* **Verify before you claim.** A green check you cannot make fail is not a check. For each fix,
  show the test failing on the old code and passing on the new.

## Done means

1. the gate/table named in your job file is **gone or widened**, and the owner rule holds;
2. a test that **fails on the pre-fix code** and passes after — quote both runs;
3. the file you edited is listed with `file:line` **before and after**;
4. `REPORT.md`-style notes in your session dir: what you changed, what you tried that failed,
   anything the docs did not tell you;
5. a reply to the owner naming the numbers: how many metaclasses are now reachable that were not
   before, and how you measured it.

---

# Job 03 — stop dropping the model, and stop offering types that do not exist

Three small, independent fixes. **All three are deletions.** Together they are the difference
between Axiomat exporting a model and exporting an empty file.

## 3a. `exportComposition` drops every element that is not `PartUsage` — **worst in this set**

`packages/backend/src/validation/exportComposition.ts:184-196`

```ts
for (const node of model.nodes) {
  if (node.type !== 'PartUsage') continue;      // ← bare continue: no counter, no warning
```

`:198-224` does the same with `if (rel.type !== 'ConnectionUsage') continue;` (and `:168`,
`:175` filter on `SubjectMembership`/`OwningMembership`).

**Effect: a model built from `PartDefinition`, `ItemUsage`, `ActorUsage` or `StateUsage` exports
an EMPTY `composition.json`. No error, no counter, no warning.** And this lands on the **Atelier
contract**, not just the UI — five sessions of prior audit never found it.

**Fix:** iterate **all** nodes into `parts[]`, carrying `type` into `CompositionPart.kind`, which
is already a free `string` at `:107`. Iterate **all** relationships into `connections[]`, leaving
`interfaceKind` **optional**. The exporter's job is projection, not selection — and only once
every crossing is exported does "does this crossing declare a kind?" become a question worth
asking, which is the whole point of the interface-kind registry Job 07 is opening.

## 3b. The check suite filters on `Satisfaction`, which is not SysML v2

`packages/backend/src/validation/checks/contracts.ts:766`

```ts
const satisfactionEdges = model.relationships.filter((r) => r.type === 'Satisfaction');
```

**`Satisfaction` does not exist in the language** — not among the 175 EClasses, not among
KerML's 82, not in the 157 index, not in any `.sysml` file in the OMG distribution. The SysML v2
name is **`SatisfyRequirementUsage`**, which is already in the relationship picker.

So `AssumptionObligationsCheck` **can never fire on a conforming model**. It reports every assumed
parameter as undischarged.

The same phantom is in three more places, which is why it survived:

| site | role |
|---|---|
| `api.ts:46` (`SYSML_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES`) | **the GUI's default relationship type** |
| `graph-connector.ts:150-151` and the schema `.describe()` at `:155` | the `create_relationship` tool **description teaches it as a "common type"** — twice, in the prose and in the schema hint (GitHub issue #32 says the same) |
| `contracts.ts:766` | the live check |

**Fix:** match `SatisfyRequirementUsage`, and keep `Satisfaction` **only as a legacy alias** for
models already written with it — the owner rule permits aliases. Fix the picker default, the
tool description and the check **in one commit**, and add a test that fails if any of the three
reverts, because each site looked locally reasonable on its own.

## 3c. Four more phantoms to remove, not to add

| phantom | where | note |
|---|---|---|
| `FlowConnectionUsage` | `api.ts:38` — offered as a **node type** | GitHub issue #31 names it; it is in no library file, no metaclass, no index entry |
| `ItemFlow` | `api.ts:47` | the real construct is `Flow`/`FlowUsage`, both already listed |
| `ExpansionRelationship` | `api.ts:52`; minted at `controlSurfaceService.ts:304`; listed at `rdfSerializer.ts:310` | an **Axiomat-internal** name sitting in a SysML vocabulary |
| `PackageDefinition`, `PackageUsage`, `ProxyPortUsage`, `ProxyPortDefinition`, `ReferenceDefinition` | `view-renderer/src/notation/shapes.ts:14-32` keyword map | 5 more; issue #31 notes the renderer draws these distinctly while the typed tool refuses them |

**Fix: delete them from the lists.** Do **not** add them to the index to make them real — they
are not SysML v2. `ExpansionRelationship` is legitimately Axiomat's own parent-link type; it
should not be offered as a *SysML relationship kind* in a picker, which is a different thing.

## Tests

* Export a model whose parts are `ItemUsage` and whose edges are `SatisfyRequirementUsage` and
  `AllocationUsage`. `parts[]` and `connections[]` are **non-empty** and the types appear
  verbatim. Before the fix both are empty.
* `AssumptionObligations` discharges a parameter against a `SatisfyRequirementUsage` edge, and is
  silent when there is genuinely no edge.
* A test asserting **no string offered in either picker is absent from the metamodel** — a
  phantom in a default is worse than a short list, because the user cannot tell.

## Note for the exporter

There is an interaction with Job 07: today `onUnknownInterfaceKind: 'skip'`
(`exportComposition.ts:207`) silently drops a connection whose kind is unknown, so the closed
8-kind list is **not** what is losing the data. Fix the projection first; the registry then has
something to validate.

---

# Host addendum, 2026-09-30 — this overrides the base above

* **Base is now `master` = `c8c6d94`, not `b5dc031`.** Master moved by the verdict-feedback
  merge (ad32e86 opened the interface-kind vocabulary and added stable ids to the export; 26447a8
  unblocked the backend build). Before you change anything, re-check your job's findings against
  `c8c6d94` and say in REPORT.md which still hold, which moved and which are already gone.
* **Job 03 overlaps the new master most:** ad32e86 changed `exportComposition` (stable ids) and the interface kinds are now open (defaults only). Build on that, do not redo it, and do not reintroduce a kind list.
* **Your worktree:** `git -C /projects/sysml-mona worktree add -b axiomat-03-exporter-20260930 /projects/axiomat-03-exporter-20260930/sysml-mona c8c6d94`
  (the shared checkout has `origin/master` = `c8c6d94` fetched; do not touch its working tree).
  Branch = `axiomat-03-exporter-20260930`. Commit there; the host pushes and merges.
* **You are a resident prime lead.** Children on `local-qwen/qwen3.8-27b` when free, else
  `openrouter-mimo/stealth/space-bunny-alpha` or `minimax-plan/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`.
  End your turn to wait for children; record them in NOTES.md under "Team". Call
  `goal.complete()` only when Done is met.
* **Other leads run in parallel** (sessions `axiomat-00-fixture-20260930`, `axiomat-03-exporter-20260930`,
  `axiomat-04-live-check-20260930`). Message another lead only if its goal is active and only
  about a real overlap — never broadcast: a broadcast revives every session and exhausted
  brain2's memory on 2026-09-30.
* The dev Axiomat instance is shared: deploy nothing into it for this job.
* Last line of REPORT.md: a "For the host" section — branch, head commit, test commands and their
  output, what to merge.

  if (node.type !== 'PartUsage') continue;      // ← bare continue: no counter, no warning
```

`:198-224` does the same with `if (rel.type !== 'ConnectionUsage') continue;` (and `:168`,
`:175` filter on `SubjectMembership`/`OwningMembership`).

**Effect: a model built from `PartDefinition`, `ItemUsage`, `ActorUsage` or `StateUsage` exports
an EMPTY `composition.json`. No error, no counter, no warning.** And this lands on the **Atelier
contract**, not just the UI — five sessions of prior audit never found it.

**Fix:** iterate **all** nodes into `parts[]`, carrying `type` into `CompositionPart.kind`, which
is already a free `string` at `:107`. Iterate **all** relationships into `connections[]`, leaving
`interfaceKind` **optional**. The exporter's job is projection, not selection — and only once
every crossing is exported does "does this crossing declare a kind?" become a question worth
asking, which is the whole point of the interface-kind registry Job 07 is opening.

## 3b. The check suite filters on `Satisfaction`, which is not SysML v2

`packages/backend/src/validation/checks/contracts.ts:766`

```ts
const satisfactionEdges = model.relationships.filter((r) => r.type === 'Satisfaction');
```

**`Satisfaction` does not exist in the language** — not among the 175 EClasses, not among
KerML's 82, not in the 157 index, not in any `.sysml` file in the OMG distribution. The SysML v2
name is **`SatisfyRequirementUsage`**, which is already in the relationship picker.

So `AssumptionObligationsCheck` **can never fire on a conforming model**. It reports every assumed
parameter as undischarged.

The same phantom is in three more places, which is why it survived:

| site | role |
|---|---|
| `api.ts:46` (`SYSML_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES`) | **the GUI's default relationship type** |
| `graph-connector.ts:150-151` and the schema `.describe()` at `:155` | the `create_relationship` tool **description teaches it as a "common type"** — twice, in the prose and in the schema hint (GitHub issue #32 says the same) |
| `contracts.ts:766` | the live check |

**Fix:** match `SatisfyRequirementUsage`, and keep `Satisfaction` **only as a legacy alias** for
models already written with it — the owner rule permits aliases. Fix the picker default, the
tool description and the check **in one commit**, and add a test that fails if any of the three
reverts, because each site looked locally reasonable on its own.

## 3c. Four more phantoms to remove, not to add

| phantom | where | note |
|---|---|---|
| `FlowConnectionUsage` | `api.ts:38` — offered as a **node type** | GitHub issue #31 names it; it is in no library file, no metaclass, no index entry |
| `ItemFlow` | `api.ts:47` | the real construct is `Flow`/`FlowUsage`, both already listed |
| `ExpansionRelationship` | `api.ts:52`; minted at `controlSurfaceService.ts:304`; listed at `rdfSerializer.ts:310` | an **Axiomat-internal** name sitting in a SysML vocabulary |
| `PackageDefinition`, `PackageUsage`, `ProxyPortUsage`, `ProxyPortDefinition`, `ReferenceDefinition` | `view-renderer/src/notation/shapes.ts:14-32` keyword map | 5 more; issue #31 notes the renderer draws these distinctly while the typed tool refuses them |

**Fix: delete them from the lists.** Do **not** add them to the index to make them real — they
are not SysML v2. `ExpansionRelationship` is legitimately Axiomat's own parent-link type; it
should not be offered as a *SysML relationship kind* in a picker, which is a different thing.

## Tests

* Export a model whose parts are `ItemUsage` and whose edges are `SatisfyRequirementUsage` and
  `AllocationUsage`. `parts[]` and `connections[]` are **non-empty** and the types appear
  verbatim. Before the fix both are empty.
* `AssumptionObligations` discharges a parameter against a `SatisfyRequirementUsage` edge, and is
  silent when there is genuinely no edge.
* A test asserting **no string offered in either picker is absent from the metamodel** — a
  phantom in a default is worse than a short list, because the user cannot tell.

There is an interaction with Job 07: today `onUnknownInterfaceKind: 'skip'`
(`exportComposition.ts:207`) silently drops a connection whose kind is unknown, so the closed

content.text:
/**
 * The interface-kind vocabulary of the exported composition document.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * ONE canonical spelling, and where it lives
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Two repos had two spellings for the same three kinds and differed by one
 * character each:
 *
 *     Axiomat (model side)   "mechanical joint"  "electrical net"  "software call"
 *     Atelier (validator)    mechanical_joint    electrical_net    software_call
 *
 * Because Atelier routes a connection to a domain plugin by exact string
 * match, no Axiomat connection ever reached an Atelier validator. The
 * failure presented as `unchecked` — the state the design reserves for a
 * genuinely unregistered kind (atelier docs/design-proof-obligations.md §3b) —
 * so a broken integration read as an honest one.
 *
 * THE DECISION: the canonical spelling is the `snake_case` identifier form,
 * and it is defined HERE, in the repo that PRODUCES the document.
 *
 *   * `composition.json` is a machine document. `interface_kind` is a key in
 *     it, and every other key in that schema (`role`, `artifact`, `contract`,
 *     `placement`, `budget_rollup`) is an identifier. A prose phrase with a
 *     space in it is not a key.
 *   * The definition cannot live in Atelier. Atelier's core is forbidden from
 *     enumerating domains: its registry is built by plugins at import time and
 *     the design's falsifiable test is that deleting every plugin leaves the
 *     core running and reporting "no domain registered"
 *     (design-proof-obligations.md §3a). A canonical *list* in Atelier would
 *     be exactly the domain enum that §3a forbids.
 *   * So the producer declares the schema's vocabulary, the consumer enforces
 *     the *syntax* of an identifier and resolves it against whatever its
 *     plugins registered. Neither side enumerates domains it does not own.
 *
 * The two sides agree by a rule that both can check without a shared file:
 * a canonical interface kind is `lower_snake_case`. Atelier can reject
 * "mechanical joint" on that rule alone, without knowing what any domain is.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Aliases
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * `LEGACY_INTERFACE_KIND_ALIASES` is the ONE explicit, tested mapping, and it
 * lives at the export boundary (see `exportComposition.ts`). It exists so a
 * model authored with the old prose spellings still exports, and so the
 * migration is visible rather than silent. It is not a second vocabulary: a
 * value that is neither canonical nor an alias is an error, never a guess.
 */

/**
 * DEFAULTS AND ALIASES ONLY. Nothing here decides what is valid.
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Owner rule, 2026-09-29, binding: **Axiomat must not restrict SysML v2
 * interface kinds.** A kind defined in the model by an `InterfaceKindDefinition`
 * node is valid because the model says it is, and a kind nobody has heard of is
 * a perfectly good kind that nobody has written a default channel list for.
 *
 * The rule is worth stating as the failure it prevents. A fixed table that
 * whitelists kinds makes SysML v2 *narrower* on Axiomat than the standard, and
 * it fails in the direction that looks healthy: an invented kind is refused at
 * export, so it never reaches Atelier, so nothing is ever reported about it,
 * and the run passes having measured nothing. A modeler who defines a
 * `bonded_ablation_interface` gets a silent hole instead of an error.
 *
 * So there are two kinds of knowledge in this file, and they are not the same:
 *
 *   * `KNOWN_INTERFACE_KINDS` -- the kinds this repo ships a DEFAULT channel
 *     list for. It saves an author from re-stating the channels everyone already

/**
 * The interface-kind vocabulary of the exported composition document.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * ONE canonical spelling, and where it lives
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Two repos had two spellings for the same three kinds and differed by one
 * character each:
 *
 *     Axiomat (model side)   "mechanical joint"  "electrical net"  "software call"
 *     Atelier (validator)    mechanical_joint    electrical_net    software_call
 *
 * Because Atelier routes a connection to a domain plugin by exact string
 * match, no Axiomat connection ever reached an Atelier validator. The
 * failure presented as `unchecked` — the state the design reserves for a
 * genuinely unregistered kind (atelier docs/design-proof-obligations.md §3b) —
 * so a broken integration read as an honest one.
 *
 * THE DECISION: the canonical spelling is the `snake_case` identifier form,
 * and it is defined HERE, in the repo that PRODUCES the document.
 *
 *   * `composition.json` is a machine document. `interface_kind` is a key in
 *     it, and every other key in that schema (`role`, `artifact`, `contract`,
 *     `placement`, `budget_rollup`) is an identifier. A prose phrase with a
 *     space in it is not a key.
 *   * The definition cannot live in Atelier. Atelier's core is forbidden from
 *     enumerating domains: its registry is built by plugins at import time and
 *     the design's falsifiable test is that deleting every plugin leaves the
 *     core running and reporting "no domain registered"
 *     (design-proof-obligations.md §3a). A canonical *list* in Atelier would
 *     be exactly the domain enum that §3a forbids.
 *   * So the producer declares the schema's vocabulary, the consumer enforces
 *     the *syntax* of an identifier and resolves it against whatever its
 *     plugins registered. Neither side enumerates domains it does not own.
 *
 * The two sides agree by a rule that both can check without a shared file:
 * a canonical interface kind is `lower_snake_case`. Atelier can reject
 * "mechanical joint" on that rule alone, without knowing what any domain is.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Aliases
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * `LEGACY_INTERFACE_KIND_ALIASES` is the ONE explicit, tested mapping, and it
 * lives at the export boundary (see `exportComposition.ts`). It exists so a
 * model authored with the old prose spellings still exports, and so the
 * migration is visible rather than silent. It is not a second vocabulary: a
 * value that is neither canonical nor an alias is an error, never a guess.
 */

/**
 * DEFAULTS AND ALIASES ONLY. Nothing here decides what is valid.
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Owner rule, 2026-09-29, binding: **Axiomat must not restrict SysML v2
 * interface kinds.** A kind defined in the model by an `InterfaceKindDefinition`
 * node is valid because the model says it is, and a kind nobody has heard of is
 * a perfectly good kind that nobody has written a default channel list for.
 *
 * The rule is worth stating as the failure it prevents. A fixed table that
 * whitelists kinds makes SysML v2 *narrower* on Axiomat than the standard, and
 * it fails in the direction that looks healthy: an invented kind is refused at
 * export, so it never reaches Atelier, so nothing is ever reported about it,
 * and the run passes having measured nothing. A modeler who defines a
 * `bonded_ablation_interface` gets a silent hole instead of an error.
 *
 * So there are two kinds of knowledge in this file, and they are not the same:
 *
 *   * `KNOWN_INTERFACE_KINDS` -- the kinds this repo ships a DEFAULT channel
 *     list for. It saves an author from re-stating the channels everyone already
 *     agrees on. A kind missing from it loses nothing but the convenience.
 *
 *   * `LEGACY_INTERFACE_KIND_ALIASES` -- spellings this repo has actually
 *     emitted, mapped to the kind they mean. It exists so a model authored
 *     before the spelling was settled still resolves to its defaults. It is a
 *     lookup, not a membership test: `isKnownInterfaceKind('quantum_link')` is
 *     false AND `resolveInterfaceKind('quantum_link')` succeeds.
 *

 * invalid" are different statements, and only the first one is ever true here.**
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Why there was a whitelist once, and what it cost
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * This file used to end in `UnknownInterfaceKindError`, thrown by the exporter,
 * backed by a canonical list. It existed for a real reason: Atelier routes a
 * connection to a domain plugin by exact string match, so a misspelled kind
 * resolved to no plugin and reported `unchecked` -- the state the design
 * reserves for honest uncertainty -- making a broken integration indistinguishable
 * from a clean one. The list was the right instinct applied to the wrong
 * question. "How do I know this kind is misspelled?" and "is this kind valid?"
 * have different answers, and a single table can only answer the first.
 *
 * Both are now answerable without the whitelist. A typo is caught by the
 * channel-completeness check, which reports an unregistered kind as a
 * NON-FATAL finding naming the kind and what it resolved to -- so a typo is
 * still visible, and an invented kind is still exported. See
 * `ChannelCompletenessCheck` in checks/contracts.ts.
 */

/**
 * The kinds this repo ships a DEFAULT channel list for.
 *
 * THIS IS NOT A WHITELIST, and it must never become one. See the header.
 */
export const KNOWN_INTERFACE_KINDS = [
  'mechanical_joint',
  'electrical_net',
  'software_call',
  'data_flow',
  'thermal_fluid',
  'power_bus',
  'logical_link',
  'security_channel',
] as const;

export type KnownInterfaceKind = (typeof KNOWN_INTERFACE_KINDS)[number];

/**
 * Legacy / authoring spellings that map onto a kind with defaults.
 *

 * "slugify anything" rule. It is a DEFAULTS lookup: resolving through it gives
 * a kind its channel list, and resolving a value that is in neither table
 * simply means "no defaults", which is not an error.
 */
export const LEGACY_INTERFACE_KIND_ALIASES: Readonly<Record<string, KnownInterfaceKind>> = {
  'mechanical joint': 'mechanical_joint',
  'electrical net': 'electrical_net',
  'software call': 'software_call',
  'data flow': 'data_flow',
  'thermal / fluid': 'thermal_fluid',
  'thermal/fluid': 'thermal_fluid',
  'power bus': 'power_bus',
  'logical link': 'logical_link',

  // (provedesign-20260928-1834q/workshop-map) declares `security channel` on
  // all nine of its connections and its own check-params.json keys the channel
  // registry on that exact string. A typo of it ('security chanel') resolves
  // to nothing, gets no defaults, and is reported by the channel check as a
  // non-fatal finding -- which is how a typo stays visible now that the
  // exporter no longer refuses it.
  'security channel': 'security_channel',
};

const KNOWN_SET: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(KNOWN_INTERFACE_KINDS);

const CANONICAL_SYNTAX = /^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)*$/;

 * It is a SUCCESS. The caller emits the kind verbatim and applies no channels.
 * The distinction from `custom` is only whether defaults were found.
 */
export type InterfaceKindResolution =
  | { kind: 'defaults'; value: KnownInterfaceKind; from?: string }

  | { kind: 'custom'; value: string }
  /** Not a usable identifier at all -- empty, or not a string. */
  | { kind: 'malformed'; value: string; suggestion: string | null };

export function isCanonicalSpelling(value: string): boolean {
  return CANONICAL_SYNTAX.test(value);
}

 * True iff this repo ships defaults for `value`.

 * The name says "known", not "valid". `false` here means no defaults, and
 * nothing more: `resolveInterfaceKind` will still succeed.
 */
export function isKnownInterfaceKind(value: string): value is KnownInterfaceKind {
  return KNOWN_SET.has(value);
}

/**
 * The closest kind-with-defaults spelling to `value`, for a hint in a warning.
 *
 * A near miss is NEVER applied to the model — it is only ever named in a
 * message. Applying it would give a connection another domain's channels and
 * then report those channels as checked, which is a worse failure than the
 * silence this replaces.
 */
export function spellingSuggestion(value: string): string | null {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || value.trim() === '') return null;

  // spelling does, and that is the common case now: since rejection is gone,
  // this warning is the only thing that will ever notice `mechanical_jointt`.

  // exactly those, so `mechanical joint` got a suggestion and
  // `mechanical_jointt` — the likelier typo — got none.
  if (slug === raw && KNOWN_SET.has(raw)) return null;

  for (const known of KNOWN_INTERFACE_KINDS) {
    if (slug.includes(known) || known.includes(slug)) return known;
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * Resolve an authored `interfaceKind` to the spelling its defaults are keyed by.
 *
 * Never throws, and never refuses. Every string comes back resolved:
 *
 *   * in the defaults table      -> `{ kind: 'defaults' }`
 *   * in the alias table         -> `{ kind: 'defaults', from }`
 *   * anything else non-empty    -> `{ kind: 'custom', value }`  <-- the case
 *     the whitelist used to reject. An invented kind is VALID; it simply has
 *     no defaults, so no channel list is applied to it and the check reports
 *     nothing about channels it has no basis to judge.
 *   * empty / not a string       -> `{ kind: 'malformed' }`, which IS a defect
 *     worth reporting: a connection with no interface kind has no meaning.
 *

 * near-miss. Guessing would silently apply another domain's channels to a
 * connection that does not have them.
 */

  if (typeof value !== 'string' || value.trim() === '') {
    return { kind: 'malformed', value: String(value ?? ''), suggestion: null };
  }
  const raw = value.trim();
  if (KNOWN_SET.has(raw)) return { kind: 'defaults', value: raw as KnownInterfaceKind };
  const aliased = LEGACY_INTERFACE_KIND_ALIASES[raw.toLowerCase()];
  if (aliased) return { kind: 'defaults', value: aliased, from: raw };
  return { kind: 'custom', value: raw };

# The denominators this scan compares every restriction against

Two, and they are different questions: what the LANGUAGE admits (metaclasses) and what the
LIBRARY ships (types). A restriction on either is a restriction on SysML v2.

## A. Language level — the 175 EClasses of the OMG pilot implementation

Source: `Systems-Modeling/SysML-v2-Pilot-Implementation`, branch `master`, file
`org.omg.sysml.model/src/main/resources/model/SysML.ecore`
(`nsURI=https://www.omg.org/spec/SysML/20250201`), fetched and saved at
`artifacts/metamodel/SysML-320.ecore`.
The companion KerML model, `org.omg.sysml.model/kerml.ecore`, is saved at
`artifacts/metamodel/kerml.ecore`; its 82 EClasses are a strict subset of the SysML 175
(verified: 0 KerML names absent from the SysML set), so **175 is the full
SysML v2 + KerML metaclass count**.

| quantity | count |
|---|---|
| EClasses total | 175 |
| of which abstract | 8 |
| concrete EClasses | 167 |
| EEnums (enumerations the language defines) | 7 |

The 8 abstract metaclasses are: ConnectorAsUsage, ControlNode, Element, Expose, Import, InstantiationExpression, LoopActionUsage, Relationship.

The 7 enums are: FeatureDirectionKind, PortionKind, RequirementConstraintKind, StateSubactionKind, TransitionFeatureKind, TriggerKind, VisibilityKind.

## B. Library level — what ships with the language

Sources, all under `artifacts/library/`:
* 21 `Systems Library/*.sysml` files (the same files the repo vendors at
  `reference-models/sysml-v2/Systems-Library/`, used for the 3 files raw.githubusercontent
  404s on),
* 37 `Domain Libraries/**/*.sysml` files from the pilot implementation.

| quantity | count |
|---|---|
| Systems Library top-level declarations (own parse, regex) | 227 |
| Domain Libraries top-level declarations (own parse, regex) | 2096 |
| distinct declared names, both libraries | 1053 |

The repo's own `packages/shared/src/sysmlv2-type-index.json` holds **157** types, generated
2026-06-29 from `third_party/SysML-v2-Release` — but that submodule is **uninitialised** in
this clone, so the index is Systems Library only. The 2026-09-11 audit
(`sysmlv2-coverage-audit-20260911-1647`) measured the same fact from the other side: the
kernel libraries and domain libraries were present but unreachable. So **157 is a subset,
and any Axiomat list compared against 157 is compared against a subset.**

Caveat on the B counts: they are a keyword regex over library files, not a parser, and are
used only as an order-of-magnitude denominator. Every restriction row in RESTRICTIONS.md is
compared against **A**, the metaclass count, which is exact.

msg="""3a: export the model, do not select a subset of it

exportComposition opened its two projection loops with

    if (node.type !== 'PartUsage') continue;
    if (rel.type !== 'ConnectionUsage') continue;

Bare continues, no counter, no warning, nothing in the document. So a model
built from ItemUsage, ActorUsage or StateUsage exported an EMPTY
composition.json and reported success, and a model whose crossings were
AllocationUsage or SatisfyRequirementUsage exported a composition with no
connections and reported success. The failure looked healthy because the
exporter and the run were looking at the same over-narrow model.

Both loops now project everything. Every node becomes a part carrying its own
SysML v2 `type` verbatim; every relationship becomes a connection carrying
its relationship `type` verbatim. `CompositionPart.kind` falls back to the
element type instead of the fixed string 'part'.

`CompositionConnection.interface_kind` becomes OPTIONAL, which is what makes
the projection possible: most SysML v2 relationships declare no interface kind
(an OwningMembership has no channels to check), and a required field is a
filter in disguise. A relationship with no kind is exported without one and
ChannelCompletenessCheck reports the gap as an error where a reader acts on
it -- so an unfinished model is distinguishable from an empty one, which is
what the old drop made impossible.

No name was added to any list. `interfaceKinds.ts` is untouched: the kind
vocabulary is already open (ad32e86) and this widens the projection, not the
vocabulary.

Tests (src/__tests__/validation/exportComposition.test.ts):
* 3 new: EVERY node; EVERY relationship (SatisfyRequirementUsage +
  AllocationUsage, the two the job names); a mixed model keeping all four
  nodes and all four relationship kinds.
* 1 inverted: 'drops a connection with no interface kind' asserted
  connections.length === 0 -- a green check standing on the defect. Now it
  asserts the crossing is projected, carries no invented kind, and is still
  reported.
* 1 amended: the lower_snake_case spelling assertion now runs over the
  connections that DECLARE a kind, since a membership declares none.

Falsified before the fix: restoring c8c6d94's exportComposition.ts and
re-running gives 4 failures (16 pass / 4 fail); with the fix, 20 pass / 0
fail. Logs in the job's session dir.
"""
open('/tmp/msg3a.txt','w').write(msg)
r=await bash(f"cd {W} && git add -A && git commit -F /tmp/msg3a.txt -q && git log --oneline -1")
print(r.output)

mod = '''/**
 * SysML v2 relationship names this repo has a WORD about.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Axiomat spent five audit sessions not finding this, because each site looked
 * locally reasonable on its own:
 *
 *   * `api.ts` offered `Satisfaction` in the relationship picker, as the
 *     default the GUI opens on;
 *   * `graph-connector.ts` described `Satisfaction` to the model-editing agent
 *     as a "common type" -- TWICE, once in the prose and once in the zod schema
 *     hint (GitHub issue #32 reports the same);
 *   * `contracts.ts` filtered live relationships on it in
 *     `AssumptionObligationsCheck`;
 *   * `verdictIngest.ts` minted it when a verdict discharged an assumption.
 *
 * **`Satisfaction` is not SysML v2.** It is not among the 175 EClasses of the
 * OMG pilot implementation's `SysML.ecore`, not among KerML's 82, not in the
 * 157-type library index, and it appears in no `.sysml` file in the OMG
 * distribution. The SysML v2 name for "this element satisfies that
 * requirement" is **`SatisfyRequirementUsage`**, which was already in the
 * picker's list three lines below the phantom.
 *
 * So `AssumptionObligationsCheck` could never fire on a conforming model: every
 * assumed parameter read as undischarged, forever, and the run reported it as a
 * finding about the MODEL rather than about the check.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE OWNER RULE, applied here
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * **Never fix by extending a list. A built-in table may give defaults and
 * aliases; it must never reject.** So nothing in this file decides what a model
 * may contain:
 *
 *   * `SATISFACTION_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE` is the spelling Axiomat WRITES. It is a
 *     default, and the only one.
 *
 *   * `LEGACY_SATISFACTION_ALIASES` is a lookup, not a membership test. It
 *     exists so a model authored before the spelling was settled -- including
 *     every model this repo's own verdict ingest wrote, and the pivot fixture --
 *     still resolves. The owner rule permits aliases explicitly.
 *
 *   * `isSatisfactionRelationship` is therefore true for the SysML v2 name and
 *     for the legacy spelling, and FALSE for everything else -- and "false"
 *     means "this is not a satisfaction edge", NOT "this relationship type is
 *     invalid". A model may contain any relationship SysML v2 defines; this
 *     function only answers which ones discharge an assumption.
 *
 * Adding a name to either array is NOT the fix for a relationship that does not
 * resolve. The fix is to make the predicate match what the language calls it.
 */

/**
 * The SysML v2 relationship type for "this element satisfies that requirement".
 *
 * Present in the 175 EClasses of the OMG pilot `SysML.ecore`
 * (nsURI https://www.omg.org/spec/SysML/20250201) as
 * `SatisfyRequirementUsage :> Usage`.
 */
export const SATISFACTION_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE = 'SatisfyRequirementUsage';

/**
 * Pre-fix spellings that mean the same thing, kept so old models keep working.
 *
 * This is an ALIAS table and nothing else: a lookup that resolves an authored
 * spelling to {@link SATISFACTION_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE}. It is never consulted to
 * decide whether a relationship is legal -- every relationship type that is not
 * in here is simply not a satisfaction edge, and stays in the model.
 *
 * `Satisfaction` is here because Axiomat itself minted it: see
 * `verdictIngest.ts`, which wrote it for every passing verdict before this
 * change, and `validation/fixtures/pivot.ts`, which still carries live edges.
 * Dropping the alias would make every model those two produced read as
 * undischarged again -- the same defect, wearing a different hat.
 */
export const LEGACY_SATISFACTION_ALIASES: readonly string[] = ['Satisfaction'];

/** Every spelling that resolves to a satisfaction edge, canonical first. */
export const SATISFACTION_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES: readonly string[] = [
  SATISFACTION_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE,
  ...LEGACY_SATISFACTION_ALIASES,
];

const SATISFACTION_SET: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(SATISFACTION_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES);

/**
 * True iff `type` is a spelling of the satisfaction relationship.
 *
 * Reads the canonical name and the legacy aliases. Everything else is false,
 * and false is not a rejection: an unrecognised relationship type flows
 * through the model untouched, it simply does not discharge an assumption.
 */
export function isSatisfactionRelationship(type: string | undefined | null): boolean {
  return typeof type === 'string' && SATISFACTION_SET.has(type);
}

/**
 * Resolve an authored relationship type to the canonical satisfaction name, or
 * `null` when it is not a satisfaction edge at all.
 */
export function asSatisfactionRelationship(type: string | undefined | null): string | null {
  return isSatisfactionRelationship(type) ? SATISFACTION_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE : null;
}
'''
